summary: Candidate A is materially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact required API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, and preserves FilesOption handling. Candidate B invents a different option API, adds explicitly forbidden association fields, duplicates Add’s request logic, and broadens the change into retry infrastructure.
reasons: A implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). B instead uses ...UploadFileOption, breaking the specified API and existing FilesOption compatibility.

A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), matching the established helper and required multipart field. B expands that helper with NewForm solely to support out-of-scope association fields.
B explicitly violates the contract by adding deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead, and project association options.

B duplicates request construction, option handling, response decoding, and missing-data behavior inside Upload instead of routing through FilesService.Add. A at least shares those mechanics through a private add method, though it also fails the literal routing requirement by bypassing Add itself and changes Add’s buffering behavior beyond the contract’s scope discipline intent/preservation requirement (despite keeping signature). Therefore A is not fully compliant but is substantially less divergent than B. Both candidates miss the required source-reader error test; A additionally lacks explicit validation coverage and uses an os.File rather than a non-seekable streamed source in its Upload retry test.
risks_a: Changes Add to eagerly read and buffer every caller-built body, which does not preserve its existing behavior and can alter memory use and error timing.
Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, contrary to the required routing.
Required validation and source-reader-failure tests are absent; its Upload retry test does not demonstrate retrying content from a non-replayable streaming reader.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong public signature and does not accept FilesOption.
Adds an entire forbidden association-option API and multipart form-field machinery.

Bypasses Add and duplicates its request/response implementation, creating future semantic drift risk and violating the single-path requirement (even though behavior currently appears copied). Maybe option handling is also changed because UploadFileOption replaces FilesOption entirely, forcing separate request-option plumbing and preventing existing FilesOption behavior from applying unchanged to Upload. The broad RawClient io.ReadSeeker retry refactor is explicitly outside scope and uses one shared seeker across attempts, increasing concurrency and lifecycle risk. Source-reader failure propagation is not tested.
